_doc: BIPOLAR corpus for .claude/hooks/lib/force-push-recovery-scope.js (orchestration-launch-ledger.md MUST-6(b)). Every `pair` holds a violation pole and a compliant pole differing in exactly ONE property — the property named in `property`. A pair whose poles do not separate is a non-discriminating instrument and the runner reds on it (instrument-bipolarity.md MUST-2). INJECTED-RESOLVER CONTRACT: `branch` / `branch_fails` drive the current-branch read; `divergence` is a uniform count OR a map from destination to count; `divergence_fails` is the UNMEASURED reason code the resolver returns; `divergence_raw` returns ok:true with a raw, possibly non-numeric count. OMITTING all three supplies NO divergence resolver, which MUST yield UNKNOWN and never clean — a pole that forgets to declare one REDS rather than passing on a measurement that never happened. THE BRANCH NAME DECIDES NOTHING: `recovery/` is MUST-6(b)'s REMEDY, not an exemption, so a diverged `recovery/lane-a` FLAGS and a zero-divergence `feat/wave-3` is CLEAN.

cases.property: the MEASURED divergence count, with the command byte-identical on both poles

poles.name: the remote holds 3 commits this clone does not
the identical command, measured at ZERO

cases.property: the divergence, NOT the destination's name — the inversion of the rejected name-based design

poles.name: a DIVERGED recovery/ branch still destroys commits
a wave branch that destroys nothing is SILENT

cases.property: whether the measured count reaches the finding, singular form included

poles.name: one remote-only commit is carried as `1 remote-only commit`
zero carries no finding at all

cases.property: whether the push is forced at all, with the divergence held at 2 on BOTH poles

poles.name: forced push over a 2-commit divergence
an ordinary push over the SAME divergence destroys nothing

cases.property: whether --force-with-lease is in the force set

poles.name: lease-force over a 2-commit divergence
no force flag, same divergence

cases.property: the short option is -f rather than -u

poles.name: -f short form
-u is not a force

cases.property: whether f appears inside the short cluster

poles.name: -fu cluster carries the force
-nu cluster carries none

cases.property: the leading + on the refspec, with no force FLAG present on either pole

poles.name: +refspec forces with NO flag present
the same refspec without the +

cases.property: the measured divergence of the refs/heads/ destination the main/master fence MISSES

poles.name: explicit refspec to main over a 4-commit divergence
the identical spelling, measured at ZERO

cases.property: whether the destination survives as a literal or is a shell expansion

poles.name: an expansion cannot be named, so it cannot be counted — UNKNOWN even with a resolver saying 0
the same shape written literally and measured at zero

cases.property: which of --force / --no-force comes last

poles.name: --no-force then --force IS a force
--force then --no-force is NOT

cases.property: whether a real force flag accompanies --force-if-includes

poles.name: --force-with-lease --force-if-includes IS a force
--force-if-includes ALONE is an ordinary push

cases.property: whether the diverged word sits in an option VALUE slot or an operand slot

poles.name: the diverged branch IS the refspec
the diverged word is --push-option's VALUE; the real target is measured at zero

cases.property: whether a force flag accompanies the bulk selector

poles.name: --all under --force names every matching ref, so no single divergence exists to count
--all alone forces nothing

cases.property: whether ANY destination in the command is measured above zero

poles.name: one measured-at-zero push does not buy silence for the other
both destinations measured at zero

cases.property: whether the nested body's push is forced

poles.name: force inside sh -c is still a force
the same nested body unforced

cases.property: whether the wrapped/retargeted invocation is forced

poles.name: env wrapper + git -C retarget
poles.command: env FOO=1 git -C /tmp/wt push --force origin feat/x

poles.name: same wrapper and retarget, no force
poles.command: env FOO=1 git -C /tmp/wt push origin feat/x

cases.property: whether the force-push text is a COMMAND or quoted prose

poles.name: a real forced push
the identical text inside a commit message body

cases.property: whether the force-push is live or commented out

poles.name: live forced push with a trailing comment
the force-push is INSIDE the comment
poles.command: git push origin feat/x # git push --force origin other

cases.property: whether the deletion is forced

poles.name: a forced deletion has NO source side, so MUST-6(b)'s command has no instantiation for it
an ordinary delete needs no force

cases.property: whether the destination is a branch or a tag

poles.name: a forced tag update replaces the tag object, so the branch-divergence measurement does not apply
the fully-qualified BRANCH of the same name, measured at zero

cases.property: the measured divergence of the destination after --, with a decoy current branch on both poles

poles.name: operands after -- still carry the destination that is measured
the same operands measured at zero

cases.property: the divergence of the branch the no-refspec push resolves to

poles.name: bare `git push --force` over a 3-commit divergence
bare `git push --force` with nothing to destroy

cases.property: whether the current branch could be read at all

poles.name: an unreadable current branch is UNKNOWN, never clean
a readable branch measured at zero

cases.property: whether the tree to read HEAD and the divergence from is itself resolvable

poles.name: a -C value from an expansion leaves the tree unknown
a literal -C value resolves against the injected branch

cases.property: whether a divergence resolver was supplied at all

poles.name: NO resolver measured nothing, so the verdict is UNKNOWN and never clean
a resolver that answered zero

cases.property: whether the source branch has a configured upstream to measure against

poles.name: no upstream is a NAMED unreadable, not a zero
an upstream that resolved and measured zero

cases.property: whether this clone holds a remote-tracking ref for the destination

poles.name: a missing remote-tracking ref is a NAMED unreadable, not a zero
a tracking ref that resolved and measured zero

cases.property: whether the git subprocess completed at all

poles.name: a failed git read is a NAMED unreadable, not a zero
a git read that completed and measured zero

cases.property: whether an ok:true resolver's count is actually a number

poles.name: ok:true carrying a non-numeric count is UNKNOWN, never clean — success is not an answer
ok:true carrying a readable zero
